theater: 西西里西部塞巴斯托與埃里克斯山

battle.name: 第一次西西里奴隸起義
battle.theater: 西西里西部塞巴斯托與埃里克斯山
battle.brief: 公元前135年，西西里島西部塞巴斯托、埃里克斯山與特拉帕尼鹽池一帶的奴工起事，擁立敘利亞裔埃努斯為王，席捲墨西拿，戰事延續四年，到前132年被羅馬執政官平定。卡面的埃及長矛屬早期青銅時代型制，比這場戰爭早三千餘年，並未出現在埃里克斯山城。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 西元前135年的這場起事，發生在羅馬共和國直轄的行省西西里島西部，性質不是國家之間的戰爭，而是羅馬治下的一次大規模武裝叛亂。起義方是島上的奴工隊伍，主力來自塞巴斯托、埃里克斯山麓、特里阿拉與利利拜周邊的大莊園、礦場與鹽田；這些奴工多為前241年羅馬完成西西里征服、以及前218至前201年第二次布匿戰爭中被俘並轉售的迦太基人、希臘人與敘利亞人，語言與出身彼此不同，平時被混編在同一批勞動隊伍裡，由莊園主派出的監督與打手驅使。據狄奧多羅斯《歷史文庫》，起義的爆發與擴張以埃里克斯山一帶為核心，埃努斯以數十數百人起事，奪得山寨後旬月之間聚眾逾萬，各鄉鎮的莊園守備與莊頭陸續被襲擊，隊伍向墨西拿與內陸丘陵擴散，形成有分隊、有首領、有王號的武裝力量。應對方是羅馬共和國：元老院接到駐島軍團的求援後，於前134年起派遣執政官級部隊登陸，戰事在幾個戰季裡反覆拉鋸，至前132年才以圍攻埃里克斯與大批投降收場；軍隊以西西里東岸的墨西拿為主要補給與集結港，機關、工兵與隨軍工匠隨軍同行。島上數十家希臘化城市的公民地主，即擁有巨型莊園的奴主階層，因莊園遭襲與勞動人口流失而受直接衝擊；沿海小城與拉丁盟邦則各自選擇自保或求援。整場衝突沒有第三國介入，也沒有形成跨海聯盟，它自始至終是行省內部的叛亂與鎮壓。
countriesEn: The revolt of 135 BC broke out in the western part of Sicily, a province of the Roman Republic, and it was in nature not a war between states but a large-scale armed rebellion inside Roman territory. The insurgents were the plantation gangs of the island, concentrated on the great estates, the mines and the salt pans around Segesta, the slopes of Eryx, Triara and Lilybaeum. Most of them were Carthaginians, Greeks and Syrians captured and resold in the course of the Roman conquest of Sicily completed in 241 BC and of the Second Punic War fought between 218 and 201 BC; they differed in language and origin, yet were mixed indiscriminately into the same labour gangs and driven by the overseers and thugs appointed by the estate owners. According to Diodorus Siculus, the outbreak and the spread of the revolt were centred on the area of Mount Eryx. Eunus rose with a few score or a few hundred men, and after seizing the hill fort his numbers grew past ten thousand within a few weeks; estate garrisons and overseers were killed one after another across the townships, and the bands spread towards Messana and the interior hills, forming an armed force with separate bands, named leaders and a royal title. The opposing side was the Roman Republic: after the senate received the appeal of the garrison in the island, consular-scale troops were sent over from 134 BC onwards, the war dragged through several campaigning seasons, and only in 132 BC did it end with the siege of Eryx and a mass surrender. The army used Messana on the eastern shore of Sicily as its main supply and assembly port, with engineers, siege craftsmen and their gear travelling with the columns. The citizen landowners of the island's several dozen Hellenic cities, the slave-owning class that held the great estates, were hit directly by the raids and by the loss of their labour force, while the small coastal towns and the Latin allies chose between self-help and an appeal for help. No third country intervened and no alliance was formed across the sea; from beginning to end this was a rebellion and its suppression within a province.
people: 起義軍方面的領袖，狄奧多羅斯留下的記載不止一個名字。核心人物是埃努斯，據說是敘利亞裔，原為西西里莊園的奴工，熟悉地形又嫻於手腕，前135年在鹽池地帶率先舉事，殺死莊頭與守備、奪得兵器與糧食，隨即被部眾推為王，踞埃里克斯山城為據，後又攻下山下的港鎮特里阿拉。另一位首領阿佩列斯在島內別處起兵，率眾響應，使莊園線遭到連續襲擊；傳記還提到阿克拉加斯方面的首領提隆，據說死於自己人的猜忌。決定勝負的關鍵人物則是埃努斯的副手法米亞斯：前133年他被困埃里克斯，走投無路之下率數百人出城投降，羅馬許以公民權與土地安置，消息傳開後大批義軍隨之放下武器，讓原本可能長期化的抵抗迅速瓦解。埃努斯本人最終在埃里克斯被俘，據說死於羅馬士兵爭奪懸賞的刺殺，屍首被斬下送往羅馬。羅馬方面，主導平叛的是元老院派遣的執政官級將領，其中西庇奧·埃米利安諾斯以在西西里平亂的政績知名，並參與其後赴島的十人委員會；公元前133年當選執政官的提比留斯·森普羅尼奧·格拉庫斯則是與西西里土地問題直接相關的人物。直接受影響最深的是島上的奴主階層與依附他們的市民：起義奪走大批勞動人口與農具，事後的清查與產權重劃直接改變了島上的土地分配格局。
peopleEn: More than one leader name is preserved for the insurgents in Diodorus Siculus. The central figure is Eunus, said to be of Syrian origin, a slave on a Sicilian estate who knew the ground well and was deft at managing people; in 135 BC he was the first to rise in the salt-pan districts, killing the overseers and the guards and seizing arms and provisions, and he was at once acclaimed king by his followers, holding the fortress of Eryx as his base and later taking the port town of Triara below the mountain. A second commander, Apelles, rose in another part of the island and answered the call, keeping up a rolling series of attacks along the estate belt; the narrative also mentions Theron, a leader in the Agrigentum district, who is said to have been killed by his own men out of jealousy. The figure who decided the outcome was Phameas, Eunus's deputy: trapped at Eryx in 133 BC, with no way out he came out of the mountain with several hundred followers and surrendered, and the Romans granted him citizenship and an allocation of land; once the news spread, large numbers of the insurgents laid down their arms, and a resistance that might have dragged on for years collapsed. Eunus himself was finally taken at Eryx and is said to have been killed by a Roman soldier competing for the reward, his head being cut off and sent to Rome. On the Roman side the suppression was directed by consular commanders dispatched by the senate; among them Scipio Aemilianus was noted for his success in Sicily and took part in the ten-man commission that later went to the island. Tiberius Sempronius Gracchus, consul in 133 BC, was the man most directly connected with the land question in Sicily. Those most deeply affected were the slave-owning class of the island and the citizens dependent on them: the revolt took away a large part of the labour force and of the farm tools, and the later inspection and redefinition of property rights directly altered the pattern of landholding on the island.
kits: 卡面兵器是「埃及長矛」：早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭以繩束綁於木杆，供守城與野戰時戳刺、格擋。這件兵器比西西里起義早了三千兩百年，並未出現在埃里克斯山中，這一點必須先說清楚。把它放進這場戰爭，是因為它標示出「矛」這一件最古老、最普遍的冷兵器技術譜系：木杆前端裝金屬矛頭，靠戳、擋、投擲發揮作用，而西西里義軍手上的武器恰恰停留在同一譜系的原始形態。義軍的實際裝備以農具與日常工具為主：削尖的木棍、折斷的農用長柄鋤、漁叉、耙、鐮刀，以及從莊園工具房裡奪得的少量鐵矛；沒有制式鎧甲，多數人穿著粗麻衣，護身靠門板、藤條編的盾或農具的護手部分。石製與鉛製的投擲物、拋石手用的石彈也在義軍名錄裡出現，用來對付羅馬的陣列。羅馬方面則是全套軍備：pilum 重型標槍配小圓盾，hasta 矛配 scutum 大盾，gladius Hispaniensis 西班牙短劍，galea 頭盔與鎖子甲，工兵帶著雲梯、撞柱與攻城塔；騎兵人數有限，只在巡邏、警戒與護送糧隊時派上用場。運輸方面，羅馬以墨西拿與利利拜兩個港口為基地，用沿海船隊輸送糧秣、木料與援兵；義軍幾乎全靠步行，靠劫掠莊園取得糧食，以驢騾負重，把鹽池提煉出的鹽作為唯一的商品收入。埃里克斯山城本身提供了水源、堅固的城牆與難以強攻的地形，是義軍能夠堅持數年的關鍵，而羅馬最後也正是靠封鎖與分化，而不是靠一次強攻拿下它。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card is the Egyptian spear: a spear of the Early Dynastic period, with a copper or bronze head lashed to a wooden shaft, used for stabbing and bracing in the defence of walls and in the open field. It predates the Sicilian revolt by more than three thousand years and never appeared on the mountain of Eryx, and that has to be said first. It is placed in this war because it marks the oldest and most widespread family of cold weapons, the spear, made of a wooden shaft with a metal head at the front and worked by stabbing, parrying and throwing; and the weapons in the hands of the Sicilian insurgents remained at a primitive stage of exactly the same family. The actual equipment of the rebels was drawn from farm tools and everyday implements: sharpened poles, the shafts of long-handled hoes broken down, fish-hooks, rakes, sickles, and a small number of iron spears taken from the estate tool-sheds. They had no standard armour, most wore coarse linen, and their protection came from door panels, wicker shields, or the hand-guards of farm implements. Stone and lead missiles and sling-stones also appear in the rebel inventory, used against the Roman battle line. The Romans, by contrast, brought the full military set: the heavy pilum with the small round shield, the hasta with the large curved scutum, the gladius Hispaniensis, the galea helmet and mail armour, while the engineers carried scaling ladders, battering rams and siege towers. Cavalry was few in number and used mainly for patrols, for pickets and for escorting supply columns. On the logistics side the Romans used the harbours of Messana and Lilybaeum as bases, moving grain, timber and reinforcements by sea; the insurgents marched on foot, obtained food by raiding estates, and used donkeys and mules for burden, with the salt harvested from the pans as their only marketable product. The fortress of Eryx itself, with its water supply, its massive wall and its difficult approach, was the key to the rebels' ability to hold out for years, and it was by blockade and division, not by a single assault, that the Romans finally took it.
tactics: 起義之所以能席捲西西里西部，靠的是一套針對莊園防衛的游擊辦法。義軍不急於攻城：先在鹽田、礦場與收割季節同時動手，把分散的勞動隊伍一併裹挾，消滅莊頭、監工與守夜的武裝，奪取糧倉裡的穀物、橄欖油、酒與農具，再退入丘陵與山寨。埃里克斯山上的古堡是最早的據點，山道狹窄、牆體厚實、水源不易被斷，義軍在山腰築牆設障，把平地交給羅馬，把垂直的岩石留給自己。當義軍進逼墨西拿時，採取了真正的圍城姿態：切斷城郊道路、攻擊城內的羅馬駐軍與商隊，同時避免與羅馬海援正面交鋒，因為他們沒有艦船。碰上羅馬縱隊在開闊地上推進，義軍避免正面對撞，改以兩翼擾亂、夜間襲擊與占據高地後投射的簡易投石製造騷擾，靠速度與地形保持主動。羅馬的反制則完全是另一套邏輯：執政官級大軍在島上展開，穩紮營寨、建造圍城工事，先用騎兵與輕步兵切斷義軍與莊園之間的補給線，再以封鎖代替強攻，重點是斷水、斷糧、斷鹽池的收益，逼山寨裡的人自己出來。分化是關鍵一招：對願意放下武器者給予公民權與土地，羅馬甚至讓已經投降的義軍首領法米亞斯出面招撫，很快就有大批隊伍倒戈。殘局階段，義軍失去補給與士氣，首領相繼被殺或被俘，餘部在山中被逐一清剿，一部分自焚，一部分被解為奴隸發賣。
tacticsEn: What allowed the revolt to sweep the western half of Sicily was a form of guerrilla war aimed at the defence arrangements of the estates. The insurgents did not hurry to storm towns: they struck simultaneously in the salt pans, the mines and at harvest time, gathering the scattered labour gangs in one stroke, eliminating the overseers, the drivers and the armed watch, seizing grain, olive oil, wine and tools from the storehouses, and then falling back into the hills and the hill forts. The old stronghold on Eryx was the earliest base; its tracks are narrow, its walls are massive and its water is hard to cut off, so the insurgents built further walls and barriers across the slope, leaving the flat ground to the Romans and keeping the vertical rock for themselves. When they pressed towards Messana they adopted a genuine siege posture: cutting the roads outside the city, striking the Roman garrison and the merchant columns inside, while carefully avoiding a set-piece naval engagement, since they possessed no ships. When the Roman columns advanced across open ground they avoided a head-on clash, relying instead on harassment from both flanks, on night attacks and on simple stone-throwing from the high ground they occupied, keeping the initiative through speed and through terrain. The Roman counter was built on entirely different logic: the consular army deployed across the island, dug in with camps and built siege works, cut the insurgents' lines of supply back to the estates with cavalry and light infantry, and then substituted blockade for assault, concentrating on cutting water, food and the revenue from the salt pans, so as to force the men in the mountain to come out. Division was the decisive move: those ready to give up their arms were offered citizenship and land, and the Romans even used Phameas, an insurgent leader who had already surrendered, to spread the word, and large numbers of bands changed sides as a result. In the closing phase the insurgents lost their supplies and their nerve, their leaders were killed or taken one after another, the remnants were hunted down in the hills, some burned themselves to death and some were sold off as slaves.
data: 能夠核實的數字有限，以下幾組最為可靠。戰役自公元前135年起，到公元前132年方告平定，前後約四年，是羅馬第一次面對大規模奴隸軍的實戰。起義的爆發點是西西里西部特拉帕尼與馬爾薩拉一帶的鹽池，夏季高溫下工作的奴工最為集中，古代記載亦把首義地點繫於埃里克斯山一帶的山寨。起事初期，埃努斯手中的骨幹人數不過數十數百；奪取山寨、殺散莊園守備之後，旬月之間聚眾以萬計，其後全島各處響應者合計達數萬人，仍沒有可以確切的總數。狄奧多羅斯留下兩組具體數字：法米亞斯率數百人投誠後，約兩萬人隨之投降；殘餘的義軍首領自殺或被殲，約五千人先後被解為奴隸，連同此前被俘者一併送往市場發賣，羅馬在西西里因此大批補入奴工，島上奴籍人口結構為之改觀。軍力方面，羅馬投入的是執政官級部隊，即兩支軍團加上騎兵與援軍的常備規模，單支軍團的步兵通常在四千至五千五百人之間，另配相當數量的輕步兵、投石手與攻城工匠。距離與後勤：墨西拿至埃里克斯直線約二百六十公里，至塞巴斯托約二百三十公里，島上沒有可供大軍縱深調度的連續驛道，羅馬的糧秣靠墨西拿與利利拜的船運以及沿海岸的強行徵集維持，義軍的糧食則來自劫掠莊園所得，難以持久。鹽田產量與莊園規模的具體數字沒有留下可靠記錄，古代作者往往只以「極多」形容，這類形容不能當作精確的產能數字使用。
dataEn: Only a limited number of figures can be verified, and the following groups are the most reliable. The war began in 135 BC and was not settled until 132 BC, roughly four years in all, and it was the first time Rome had to face a large slave army in the field. The point of outbreak was the belt of salt pans around Trapani and Marsala in western Sicily, where the gangs were most concentrated during the summer heat, and the ancient narrative likewise places the first rising around the hill forts of Eryx. At the start the hard core in Eunus's hands numbered only a few score or a few hundred; after the forts were taken and the estate guards were broken up, the numbers ran past ten thousand within a few weeks, and the total of those answering the call from all over the island reached tens of thousands, with no exact figure surviving. Diodorus preserves two concrete numbers: after Phameas surrendered with several hundred men, about twenty thousand followed him in laying down their arms; the surviving leaders then killed themselves or were destroyed, and roughly five thousand were sold off as slaves, together with those previously captured, so that Rome refilled the island's stock of slave labour and the composition of the servile population changed. On the Roman side the force committed was of consular scale, that is, two legions with cavalry and reinforcements at permanent strength, a single legion normally numbering between four thousand and five thousand five hundred foot, besides light infantry, slingers and siege engineers. Distance and logistics: the straight line from Messana to Eryx is about two hundred and sixty kilometres and to Segesta about two hundred and thirty; the island has no continuous made road for the deep redeployment of a large army, and the Roman grain was maintained by sea transport out of Messana and Lilybaeum together with forcible requisition along the coast, while the insurgents' food came from what they could seize on the estates and could not be sustained. The output of the salt pans and the size of the estates leave no reliable figures; the ancient writers tend to describe them as extremely numerous, and such descriptions cannot be used as precise measures of production.
cause: 起義的成因可以分三層看。最下層是羅馬的戰爭機器：前264至前241年的第一次布匿戰爭，最後以迦太基放棄西西里告終，島上大量城邦人口淪為戰俘；前218至前201年的第二次布匿戰爭又帶來新一批俘虜，這些人經由市場被賣到島內的大莊園，集中在西部的塞巴斯托、埃里克斯山麓、特里阿拉與利利拜周邊，形成一批來源複雜、人數眾多的奴工隊伍。第二層是土地與勞動的集中：島內土地兼併成巨型莊園，莊園主以極少數人控制大片土地與上千名勞動者，莊園主要靠奴工耕作、採鹽、榨油，農產品因此流向羅馬與希臘化城市市場，本地小農與自耕者被擠壓。第三層是直接引爆的待遇與觸發事件：奴工被烙上烙印以防逃亡、禁止婚配、禁止祭祀、不得持有任何財物；莊園主在豐收年份把口糧由甲等降到乙等，遇上歉收年頭再削減，饑餓與死亡成為常態；而西西里淪為行省之後，島上自由民小地主與大城市奴主之間的爭鬥、希臘化城市與迦太基城市歸順者之間的地位落差，還有前134至前133年間當局對島上矛盾的仲裁不足，都讓爆發不再需要額外的導火線。鹽池裡的高溫勞作、鹽的收成季節，以及一批待發配的戰俘或被沒收的財產在莊園之間調動，正是狄奧多羅斯記錄的起義引爆時刻。一旦莊頭與監工被殺，逐級的模仿便沿著莊園的網絡迅速擴散。
causeEn: The causes of the revolt can be read on three levels. The lowest is Rome's war machine: the First Punic War, fought from 264 to 241 BC, ended with Carthage giving up Sicily, and the populations of the island's cities fell into Roman hands as prisoners of war; the Second Punic War of 218 to 201 BC produced a new crop of captives, and these people were sold through the markets onto the great estates of the island, concentrated in the west around Segesta, the foot of Eryx, Triara and Lilybaeum, forming a large and ethnically mixed body of slave labour. The second level is the concentration of land and labour: holdings merged into huge plantations, and a very few owners controlled vast tracts and hundreds or thousands of workers; the estates produced grain, oil and salt for the Roman and Hellenic markets, while local smallholders and free peasants were squeezed out. The third level is the treatment and the trigger: slaves were branded to prevent escape, forbidden to marry, forbidden to worship and allowed to own nothing; in good years the masters cut their ration from the first grade to the second, and in a poor year cut it again, so that hunger and death were routine. And with Sicily now a Roman province, the quarrel between the small free landowners of the island and the great city slave-owners, the gap in status between the Hellenic and Carthaginian cities and their surrendered inhabitants, and the weak arbitration by the authorities in 134 and 133 BC all meant that the outbreak needed no further fuse. Work in the salt pans under summer heat, the salt harvest season, and the movement of captured or confiscated property between estates were the moment the ancient narrative marks for the outbreak. Once the overseers and the drivers were killed, the imitation spread from estate to estate along the network of the plantations.
impact: 這場起義在西西里留下的痕跡，比它本身的戰役規模更深。其一，奴隸大軍第一次證明可以組織成有國王、有分隊、有據點的軍隊，羅馬此後再遇到奴軍，便不再當作零散治安事件處理，而是以執政官與執政官級大軍回應；這套辦法在四十年後的第二次西西里奴隸戰爭、以及前73年起的第三次奴隸戰爭中反覆被複製，成為羅馬對付奴隸起義的固定戰術範本。其二，奴源枯竭改變了島上的經濟結構：戰後大批島民被解為奴隸重新流入市場，又有一批莊園失去勞動力，奴價與地價都受影響；前132年元老院組成的十人委員會在西西里清查土地與奴籍，把部分土地分給作戰有功的獲釋奴隸，形成一批小有產的奴籍自由農，長期影響島上的土地分配與政治。其三，這場戰爭與羅馬本土的政治震動同時發生：西庇奧·埃米利安諾斯以在西西里平亂的經歷，主張把西西里各城的忠誠公民納入羅馬的政治秩序；提比留斯·森普羅尼奧·格拉庫斯則於前133年提出土地法，主張把公地分給無地者。西西里的奴亂於是被解讀為「土地被少數人兼併、勞動力被榨取」這個結構性問題的徵兆，相關觀察直接進入羅馬本土關於土地改革的辯論，農業兼併、兵源枯竭與地中海世界的奴隸供應被連成一條線。其四，在軍事上，羅馬此後更倚重常備軍與兵役營制，重新編排鎮壓外省與供應首都的關係；西西里則從一個靠奴工維繫的大莊園經濟，逐步轉為以奴籍自由農與小農為主的形態，這個轉變既解除了危機，也埋下新的矛盾。其五，在武器史的層面，這場戰爭留下清晰的對照：以削尖木棍與農具為主的起義軍裝備，與羅馬的制式標槍、長矛、盾牌、短劍與鎧甲在同一場戰鬥裡相撞，反襯出羅馬的軍備優勢並不只來自訓練，也來自幾千年累積的金屬冶煉與工兵制度。
impactEn: The traces the revolt left in Sicily run deeper than the scale of the fighting itself. First, a slave army had proved for the first time that it could be organised into a force with a king, separate bands and fixed bases, and the Romans no longer treated such a rising as a local policing matter, answering it with a consul and with a force of consular scale; the method was copied in the second Sicilian slave war forty years later and in the third slave war from 73 BC, and became the standing Roman doctrine for slave revolts. Second, the drying up of the slave supply changed the structure of the Sicilian economy: after the war large numbers of islanders were returned to the market as slaves, and a number of estates lost their labour force, so both slave prices and land values were affected; in 132 BC the senate set up a commission of ten men which inspected the land and the register of slaves in Sicily and allotted part of the land to the freed slaves who had served in the fighting, producing a class of small slave-born freeholders whose effect on landholding and on the politics of the island lasted a long time. Third, the revolt ran at the same moment as the political agitation in Rome itself: Scipio Aemilianus, from his experience of the Sicilian campaign, argued for admitting the loyal citizens of the Sicilian cities into the Roman political order, while Tiberius Sempronius Gracchus put forward his land law in 133 BC, calling for the public land to be distributed to the landless. The Sicilian revolt was therefore read as a symptom of the structural problem of land concentrated in a few hands and of labour squeezed dry, and the observation fed directly into the Roman debate on agrarian reform, joining together the consolidation of farms, the drying up of the military manpower levy and the supply of slaves across the Mediterranean. Fourth, militarily, Rome henceforth relied more heavily on standing forces and on the organisation of the service, rearranging the link between suppressing the provinces and provisioning the capital, while Sicily moved gradually from an economy sustained by slave labour towards one made up of slave-born freeholders and small farmers, a change that relieved the crisis and at the same time planted new conflicts. Fifth, at the level of the history of weapons, the war leaves a sharp contrast: the insurgent equipment of sharpened poles and farm tools set against the Roman standard pilum, spear, shield, sword and armour in the same fighting shows that the Roman advantage in arms rested not only on training but also on several thousand years of accumulated metalworking and on an engineers' system.
result: 公元前132年，義軍在埃里克斯山被平定。埃努斯於最後的圍困中被俘，據古代記載，他是在突圍或被追殺的過程中死於羅馬士兵的刀下，屍首被斬下送往羅馬；其部眾或死於山中，或在逃亡途中被殺，也有不少人主動放下武器，約兩萬人隨法米亞斯的榜樣投降；最後一批拒絕投降者退入山林自焚或被搜捕出來，約五千人被解為奴隸送往市場，另有大批人淪為羅馬的俘獲與刑罰對象。戰爭結束後，元老院沒有把西西里當作尋常行省處理：前132年組成的十人委員會赴島實地勘察，聽取城市公民、莊園主與獲釋奴隸三方陳述，重新界定公地與私地的界線，處理前線戰俘的歸屬，並把部分土地分給作戰有功或已經獲釋的奴籍居民，藉此削弱大莊園的壟斷。羅馬在島上重建了秩序：以執政官為中心的鎮壓模式確立，沿海港口的補給線固定下來，山寨逐一清剿，鹽田與礦場的勞動重新編排。此後西西里沒有再出現同樣規模的起義，直到前104年第二場奴隸戰爭重新點燃。對起義者而言，他們沒有得到獨立的國家，卻迫使羅馬第一次正視奴隸軍作為一支軍隊的事實；對羅馬而言，這場戰爭的代價是四個戰季的兵役、一批再也不能回到島上的人，以及一場幾乎改變西西里土地結構的清查。
resultEn: In 132 BC the insurgents were broken at Eryx. Eunus was taken in the final siege and, according to the ancient account, was killed by a Roman soldier's blade in the course of the flight or the pursuit, his head being cut off and carried to Rome. His followers either died in the mountain or were killed on the road, and many laid down their arms, about twenty thousand surrendering on the example set by Phameas; the last to refuse surrendered were driven back into the hills, where they burned themselves or were hunted out and taken, and about five thousand were sold off as slaves, while many others fell into the hands of Rome as captives and objects of punishment. When the war was over the senate did not treat Sicily as an ordinary province: the commission of ten formed in 132 BC went to the island, heard the three parties in person, redrew the line between public and private land, settled the status of the prisoners taken in the fighting, and allotted land to the slave-born residents who had earned it or had already been freed, so as to weaken the grip of the great estates. Rome rebuilt order on the island: the model of suppression centred on the consul was established, the supply lines of the coastal harbours were fixed, the hill forts were cleared one by one, and the labour of the salt pans and the mines was rearranged. No rising of the same size came to Sicily again until the second slave war began in 104 BC. The insurgents gained no state of their own, but they forced Rome for the first time to face a slave army as an army; the price Rome paid was four campaigning seasons, a number of men who would never come back to the island, and an inspection that came close to rewriting the structure of Sicilian landholding.
